title: Economics story assets for the concise research memo
central_argument: Profit depends on the completed job, its programme and payer, and retained obligation. App activity and large datasets do not identify those economics.
scope: Six concise visual-page briefs only. No strategy selection, budget, ROI forecast or implementation. The user-provided visual reference contributes design hierarchy only, never case facts.
evidence_audit: Supplied caseP&L, observed external portfolio counts, published programme terms, dated retail estimates and constructed risk states remain explicitly distinct.

pages.headline: After-sales provides 46.7% of case gross profit from 13.0% of revenue.
pages.body: The supplied case assigns Rp3,150 billion of gross profit to services, spare parts and body and paint, against Rp9,000 billion of revenue. Vehicle sales remain the largest individual profit pool. This makes the economics of completed ownership jobs material even when they generate fewer app sessions. The four lines belong to one case P&L, not four customer samples. A programme still needs incremental contribution after its own costs.

pages.headline: Toyota and Lexus xEV sales fell 6,025 units as portfolio scale and mix both decreased.
pages.body: Astra reports 37,693 Toyota and Lexus xEV sales in 2024 and 31,668 in 2025. The symmetric accounting bridge assigns about 5,050 fewer units to the total-portfolio scale term and 975 to its xEV mix term. Averaging both calculation orders removes an arbitrary ordering choice. These terms reconcile the observed change; they do not measure the effects of national demand, Digiroom or any proposed solution.

pages.headline: A longer programme maximum can cover fewer service events and different parts benefits.
pages.body: Current Toyota material gives T-CARE seven scheduled labor-and-parts events within three years or 60,000 km. T-CARE Lite covers labor for seven events; its parts package is separate. Legacy GBSB allows six events within four years or 50,000 km. Its published calendar lists events through month 30. Headline years therefore do not identify covered visit count, the customer’s actual payment date or dealer gross profit. Eligibility and specified work still govern.

pages.headline: The bZ4X tool’s four later-service estimates total Rp9.101 million on a March 2024 basis.
pages.body: The public Toyota tool lists bZ4X Panoramic View estimates from Rp847,000 at visits 8 and 10 to Rp3,713,000 at visit 11. Labor and parts sum to Rp9,101,000 across the four events. The opened note dates these estimates to March 2024 and allows dealer and additional-work differences. These are useful illustrations of uneven bills, not current invoices, total ownership cost, dealer margin or a forecast of customer spending.

pages.headline: A Rp10 million top-up leaves a Rp160 million offer below a Rp200 million floor.
pages.body: In this constructed example, the capped top-up adds Rp10 million to a Rp160 million offer, producing Rp170 million of customer credit. A separate full-floor promise requires Rp200 million. Its Rp40 million shortfall leaves Rp25 million with the dealer after the assumed Rp15 million insurer layer, using a Rp10 million retention. That arithmetic excludes contribution and running costs. No actual policy, underwriting appetite or approved Auto2000 offer is established.

pages.headline: The same pooled offers create higher peak retained losses when low valuations arrive together.
pages.body: These constructed worlds use the same twenty units and the same pooled low and high offers across two stress states. Dispersion puts ten low offers in each state; synchronization puts all twenty in one. Under the assumed Rp100 million aggregate recovery limit, the highest dealer residual rises from Rp300 million to Rp700 million. No probability is assigned. This exposes a limit of per-unit reasoning without estimating actual correlation, expected loss or insurance availability.
pages.evidence_label: ILLUSTRATIVE JOINT STRESS STATES • NO PROBABILITIES OR EXPECTED-LOSS ESTIMATE
